    // The yaw-pitch-roll decomposition of a quaternion, in ZXY order (roll,
    // then pitch, then yaw — the order CreateFromYawPitchRoll applies). At the
    // gimbal-lock poles (pitch = +-90 degrees) yaw and roll are not unique.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_between_quaternions_and_Euler_angles
    EulerAngles(q: Quaternion): EulerAngles {
        var n = q.Normalize;
        var pitch = (2.0 * (n.W * n.X - n.Y * n.Z)).Clamp(-1.0, 1.0).Asin;
        var yaw = (2.0 * (n.X * n.Z + n.W * n.Y)).Atan2(1.0 - 2.0 * (n.X.Square + n.Y.Square));
        var roll = (2.0 * (n.X * n.Y + n.W * n.Z)).Atan2(1.0 - 2.0 * (n.X.Square + n.Z.Square));
        return (yaw, pitch, roll, RotationOrder.ZXY);
    }

    // The quaternion of a rotor, under the isomorphism (w, x, y, z) =
    // (Scalar, YZ, ZX, XY): each bivector plane maps to the quaternion unit
    // whose axis is perpendicular to it.
    Quaternion(r: Rotor3D): Quaternion
        => (r.Bivector.YZ, r.Bivector.ZX, r.Bivector.XY, r.Scalar);

    // The rotor of a quaternion (the inverse of the isomorphism above).
    Rotor3D(q: Quaternion): Rotor3D
        => (q.W, Bivector3D(q.X, q.Y, q.Z));

    // The rotor of an axis-angle rotation.
    Rotor3D(aa: AxisAngle): Rotor3D
        => aa.Quaternion.Rotor3D;

    // The geometric product of two rotors: the image of the Hamilton product
    // under the quaternion isomorphism, so a.Multiply(b) applies b first.
    Multiply(a: Rotor3D, b: Rotor3D): Rotor3D
        => (a.Quaternion * b.Quaternion).Rotor3D;

    // The reverse of the rotor: the opposite rotation (for a unit rotor the
    // reverse is the inverse).
    Inverse(r: Rotor3D): Rotor3D
        => (r.Scalar, Bivector3D(-r.Bivector.YZ, -r.Bivector.ZX, -r.Bivector.XY));

    // Rescale to unit magnitude, restoring the rotor invariant after repeated
    // products.
    Normalize(r: Rotor3D): Rotor3D
        => r.Quaternion.Normalize.Rotor3D;

    // Apply the rotor's sandwich product R v ~R.
    Transform(v: Vector3D, r: Rotor3D): Vector3D
        => v.Transform(r.Quaternion);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): r * v.
    Multiply(r: Rotor3D, v: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Transform(v, r);

    // Rotate a point about the origin with a rotor.
    Transform(p: Point3D, r: Rotor3D): Point3D
        => p.PositionVector.Transform(r.Quaternion).ToPoint;

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): r * p.
    Multiply(r: Rotor3D, p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Transform(p, r);

    // Rotate a point about the origin with a quaternion.
    Transform(p: Point3D, q: Quaternion): Point3D
        => p.PositionVector.Transform(q).ToPoint;

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): q * p.
    Multiply(q: Quaternion, p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Transform(p, q);

    // Rotate a unit direction.
    Transform(d: Direction3D, q: Quaternion): Direction3D
        => Direction3D(d.Vector.Transform(q));

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): q * d.
    Multiply(q: Quaternion, d: Direction3D): Direction3D
        => Transform(d, q);

    //==
    // Rotation matrices — 2D rotations embed in Matrix3x2, 3D rotations in
    // Matrix4x4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix

    // The affine matrix of a plane rotation about the origin.
    Matrix3x2(r: Rotation2D): Matrix3x2
        => Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(r.Angle);

    // The affine matrix of a rotor's rotation.
    Matrix3x2(r: Rotor2D): Matrix3x2
        => r.Rotation2D.Matrix3x2;

    // The homogeneous matrix of a quaternion's rotation.
    Matrix4x4(q: Quaternion): Matrix4x4
        => Matrix4x4.CreateFromQuaternion(q);

    // The quaternion of a rotation matrix. Precondition: the upper 3x3 block
    // is orthonormal (a pure rotation, no scale or shear).
    Quaternion(m: Matrix4x4): Quaternion
        => Quaternion.CreateFromRotationMatrix(m);

    // The homogeneous matrix of an axis-angle rotation.
    Matrix4x4(aa: AxisAngle): Matrix4x4
        => Matrix4x4.CreateFromAxisAngle(aa.Axis.Vector, aa.Angle);

    // The homogeneous matrix of chained elemental rotations.
    Matrix4x4(e: EulerAngles): Matrix4x4
        => e.Quaternion.Matrix4x4;

    // The homogeneous matrix of a rotor's rotation.
    Matrix4x4(r: Rotor3D): Matrix4x4
        => r.Quaternion.Matrix4x4;

    //==
    // # TRS transform operations
    //
    // Application, matrix interchange, and the lossy widening/narrowing between a
    // rigid pose and the TRS transforms of `transforms.types.plato`.

    //==
    // TRS transforms — scale, then rotate, then translate. Not closed under
    // composition (rotating a non-uniform scale leaves the TRS family), so
    // compose them through their matrix or affine forms.

    // Apply the transform: scale, rotate, then translate.
    Transform(p: Point2D, t: TrsTransform2D): Point2D
        => ((p.PositionVector * t.Scale).Transform(t.Rotation) + t.Translation).ToPoint;

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): t * p.
    Multiply(t: TrsTransform2D, p: Point2D): Point2D
        => Transform(p, t);

    // Apply the scale and rotation to a displacement (translation does not act
    // on vectors).
    Transform(v: Vector2D, t: TrsTransform2D): Vector2D
        => (v * t.Scale).Transform(t.Rotation);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): t * v.
    Multiply(t: TrsTransform2D, v: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => Transform(v, t);

    // The affine matrix of the transform: S * R * T in row-vector order.
    Matrix3x2(t: TrsTransform2D): Matrix3x2
        => Matrix3x2.CreateScale(t.Scale) * t.Rotation.Matrix3x2
            * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(t.Translation);

    // Compose through the affine closure. TRS is not closed under composition
    // (rotating a non-uniform scale leaves the TRS family); the product is the
    // matrix form of first-then-second, re-read as TRS with unit shear assumed.
    // Prefer AffineTransform2D.Compose when the result must stay exact.
    Compose(first: TrsTransform2D, second: TrsTransform2D): AffineTransform2D
        => AffineTransform2D(first).Compose(AffineTransform2D(second));

    // Alias for Compose, enabling the * operator: a * b applies a first.
    // Returns AffineTransform2D because TRS is not closed under composition.
    Multiply(a: TrsTransform2D, b: TrsTransform2D): AffineTransform2D
        => a.Compose(b);

    // A rigid pose widened to a TRS transform with unit scale.
    TrsTransform2D(pose: Pose2D): TrsTransform2D
        => (pose.Position.PositionVector, pose.Rotation, Number2.One);

    // The rigid part of the transform, discarding scale. Named Pose rather
    // than Pose2D because the conversion is lossy and must stay explicit.
    Pose(t: TrsTransform2D): Pose2D
        => (t.Translation.ToPoint, t.Rotation);
